trap-thesis-restatement.evidence: 'Thus, noble gases sit at ionization-energy peaks.' closes a three-sentence argument and is its conclusion, not a restatement of an already-stated thesis — the preceding sentences establish the energetic comparison, this one draws it.
trap-thesis-restatement.notes: pass on all ten. FINDING, not fixed inline: the block states as established the very mechanism its parent's authorNotes caveat records as unsupported. prop:noble-gas-characterization carries a dated caveat (2026-06-16) reporting that a 50-dps computation of the confinement shadow price sigma_F(k) along the electron-dressing chain 'does not support the Relation to ionization energy mechanism as written: sigma_F(k) decays monotonically along the chain rather than peaking at closed shells', and that the Wedderburn degeneracy standing in for 'full curls' is generic across Hecke levels rather than specific to closed shells — concluding that 'the ionization-energy and shell-closure claims are interpretations pending a categorical derivation, not results'. This block's first section is that mechanism, asserted without qualification ('The crossing energy of a closed sub-link represents a local maximum across each period ... Thus, noble gases sit at ionization-energy peaks'). The EMPIRICAL conclusion is correct — the peaks are real — so nothing here is factually wrong about chemistry; what is missing is that the categorical derivation of the peaks from crossing energy is the part the caveat says does not go through. Proposed: carry the caveat, e.g. open with 'On the interpretation of prop:noble-gas-characterization (see its caveat), ...', or mirror the caveat into this block's .ts authorNotes. Same issue, more strongly worded, on rem:noble-gas-characterization-interpretation, which says the correspondence is 'formally' bound.
